name: LTC6752IS5#TRPBF
title: 280MHz, 2.9ns single comparators, rail-to-rail input, CMOS push-pull output
summary: A family of single high-speed comparators: 2.9ns typical delay, 1.2ns edges and toggling to 280MHz on about 4.5mA. The inputs run from 0.2V below VEE to 0.1V above VCC and the push-pull CMOS output swings to the rails. The LTC6752 in TSOT-23-5 runs from one 2.45V to 3.5V supply; the LTC6752-2 (MSOP-8) and LTC6752-3 (3mm × 3mm QFN) add a separate 1.71V to 3.5V output supply with a 2.45V to 5.25V input supply, shutdown, a latch and adjustable hysteresis pin, and on the -3 a complementary output. LTC6752IS5#TRPBF is the TSOT-23 LTC6752, I grade (-40°C to 85°C), on tape and reel.

notes: The I and H grades carry the same marking; the grade is on a label on the shipping container.

tables.title: Absolute maximum ratings
notes: Note 1: Going past any of these ratings can damage the part for good; spending long periods at any of them can shorten its life and lower its reliability.

Note 2: Every input, shutdown, latch/hysteresis and output pin has reverse-biased ESD diodes. If a pin is taken more than 300mV past either supply, its current is to be held under 10mA. Guaranteed by design and/or characterization, not tested in production.
Note 3: Keeping the junction under its maximum can call for a heat sink. Guaranteed by design and/or characterization, not tested in production.
Note 4: The I grades (LTC6752I, LTC6752-2I, LTC6752-3I) are guaranteed over -40°C to 85°C, the H grades (LTC6752H, LTC6752-2H, LTC6752-3H) over -40°C to 125°C.

circuits.title: Power supply configuration (a): single supply
circuits.description: Input and output stages both run from 3V, with VEE at 0V.
notes: Applies to the LTC6752-2 and LTC6752-3.

circuits.title: Power supply configuration (b): output supply below input supply
circuits.description: The input stage runs from 5V and the output stage from 1.8V, both over a 0V VEE, so a 5V analog range drives 1.8V logic.
notes: Applies to the LTC6752-2 and LTC6752-3.

circuits.title: Power supply configuration (c): output supply above input supply
circuits.description: The input stage runs from 2.5V and the output stage from 3.5V, both over a 0V VEE.
notes: Applies to the LTC6752-2 and LTC6752-3.

circuits.title: Power supply configuration (d): negative output logic
circuits.description: VEE sits at -2.5V, the input stage at 2.5V and the output stage at 0V, so the output swings between -2.5V and 0V.
notes: Applies to the LTC6752-2 and LTC6752-3.

circuits.title: Adjusting hysteresis with an external resistor at LE/HYST
circuits.description: One resistor R from LE/HYST to VEE pulls the pin below its 1.25V open-circuit level and so raises the built-in hysteresis; a smaller R gives more hysteresis (Hysteresis vs Control Resistor).

circuits.title: Additional hysteresis using positive feedback
circuits.description: The signal drives -IN. R1 from VREF and R2 from Q meet at +IN, so each output transition pushes the +IN threshold further in the direction the signal is moving; offset and hysteresis follow equations (1) and (2). One example: on 3.0V total with VEE = 0V, VREF = 1.25V, R2 = 4.53kΩ and R1 = 511Ω add roughly 300mV of hysteresis and shift the threshold by roughly 1.275V.

circuits.title: High speed clock restoration / level translation
circuits.description: A 200MHz clock from a source on a 5V supply reaches +IN over a long trace, arriving as about 150mVP-P around 2.5V. -IN is held at VREF = VEE + 2.5V. The input stage runs at VEE + 5V and the output stage at VEE + 1.8V, so Q delivers a full 1.8V-logic clock, about 1.8VP-P, to a receiver on a 1.8V supply. The input is DC-coupled, which keeps the duty cycle of the clock.

parts.value: Clock/data source via long trace, 150mVP-P, 200MHz, VCM = 2.5V

circuits.title: Optical receiver
circuits.description: An FCI-125 photodiode, biased from 3.3V through 47.6k, feeds the inverting input of an LTC6268 FET-input op amp wired as a transimpedance stage with a 20k feedback resistor. The op amp's +IN sits at half of 3.3V from a 1k/1k divider decoupled by 0.1µF. The op amp output drives -IN of an LTC6752-2 whose +IN is a fixed threshold from a 5.49k/4.53k divider off 3.3V, decoupled by 0.1µF. The comparator runs from a single 3.3V and its Q gives a 0V to 3.3V logic output.
notes: The photodiode is lit by a light source whose intensity varies sinusoidally.

circuits.title: Pulse stretcher / monostable multivibrator
circuits.description: Two LTC6752-2 parts on 3.3V turn any input pulse of 15mV to 3.3V and at least 5ns into a 3.3V pulse of about 100ns. U1 is a threshold detector: its +IN takes the 50Ω-source input across a 49.9Ω termination, and its -IN sits near 11mV from a 15k/49.9Ω divider off 3.3V filtered by 1000pF, so the output stays low with no input. A pulse drives U1 high; through a 22k/22k/2k network this drives U2 high, and U2's output, through the diode and 1k, holds U1's +IN up. The timing capacitor C (100pF) then charges through timing resistor R (6.65k) from U2's output; after about 100ns U2 goes low and U1 is free to fall. A larger C gives a longer pulse, with no upper limit.

circuits.description: A small differential signal carrying a large common-mode component goes straight to +IN and -IN of an LTC6752-2 with VCC = 5V and VDD = 2.7V. Q recovers the differential signal: a 200MHz, 200mVP-P differential input with 2.5V of random common-mode noise is recovered, with a little output modulation from cycle-to-cycle changes in delay.

operation.text: The family has three single comparators. The LTC6752 (TSOT-23-5) has one positive supply pin and no control pins. The LTC6752-2 (MSOP-8) adds a separate output-stage supply VDD, a shutdown pin and the LE/HYST latch and hysteresis pin. The LTC6752-3 (3mm × 3mm QFN) has all of these plus a complementary output /Q. The family is a direct replacement for the ADCMP60X parts.

A rail-to-rail input stage feeds an intermediate gain stage and then an output stage driving a complementary FET pair, which takes Q to either rail. Internal signals use small swings to keep speed high at low power. On the LTC6752 the input and output supply pins are joined inside and called VCC. The LTC6752-3 has a second, inverting output stage for /Q.

On the LTC6752-2 and LTC6752-3, VCC is held 2.45V to 5.25V above VEE and VDD 1.71V to 3.5V above VEE, independently, so the analog input range and the output logic level can differ. The supplies may come up in any order provided no absolute maximum rating is exceeded. The LTC6752 runs from 2.45V to 3.5V.

The input stage is a PNP pair working from VEE - 0.2V up to roughly VCC - 1.5V (low common-mode region) and an NPN pair working from roughly VCC - 1V up to VCC + 0.1V (high region). Between VCC - 1.5V and VCC - 1V, or with one input in each region, both pairs are partly on. Offsets are trimmed and small while both inputs stay wholly in one region; in the transition band offset can grow, so DC-precise designs keep out of it.

With both inputs in the low region bias current is negative and flows out of the pins; in the high region it is positive and flows in. Large differential inputs do not raise it much: with one input at the positive rail and the other at the negative rail, either pin typically draws under 3.5µA.

The inputs survive voltages beyond VCC to VEE without outside parts. An input taken more than 300mV past a supply turns on an internal ESD diode, and a series resistor then keeps the current under 10mA. Reverse-biased ESD diodes sit on the pins and further clamps sit between the supplies. Plugging the part into a live socket can fire those clamps and pass large current between supply pins, and is not recommended.
Output current is typically ±22mA with a 2.5V output supply and ±39mA with 3.3V. A sustained output short needs care to keep the junction under 150°C.

The outputs drive 3.3V, 2.5V and 1.8V CMOS logic. VDD stays no more than 3.6V above VEE for reliability. With VDD at 3V or more the outputs meet TTL thresholds and can drive TTL logic on 5V, because all TTL levels (VIH, VIL, VOH, VOL) are at or below 2.4V.

Timing figures are given for 5pF, a standard TTL/CMOS load. Larger loads work but slow the part (see the propagation delay and toggle rate curves against load capacitance); the least possible load capacitance gives the best speed.

Built-in hysteresis is 5mV by default and stops slow, close inputs from making the output chatter. Its positive feedback also makes small-signal gain infinite at the trip points. VOS and VHYST are defined from the two trip points. On the LTC6752-2 and LTC6752-3 the LE/HYST pin raises, removes or latches it: above 1.7V hysteresis is off and gain falls to a finite value, typically 6000V/V; moving the pin from its open-circuit 1.25V down to 800mV raises hysteresis; below 0.3V the output latches.

LE/HYST behaves as 1.25V behind 20k. A single resistor from the pin to VEE is the simplest way to raise hysteresis; the Hysteresis vs Control Resistor curve gives the typical result for each value. More hysteresis again comes from positive feedback from Q to +IN.

Pulling LE/HYST below 300mV above VEE freezes the output. Setup time is how long the input must be steady before the latch edge for the right state to be held; hold time is how long it must stay steady after the edge. Releasing the latch hands the output back to the input after the latch propagation delay tPDL. An input change too close to the edge can latch the wrong state; a short input pulse that meets setup and hold is captured. A floating LE/HYST pin leaves latching off. Both LTC6752-3 outputs latch together.

SHDN (active low) on the LTC6752-2 and LTC6752-3 cuts total supply current to a typical 580µA (LTC6752-2) or 650µA (LTC6752-3) at 2.5V. In shutdown the output PFET and NFET are both off, so the outputs are high impedance. The pin must come within 600mV of VEE to shut down; left open it is pulled toward the positive supply and the part stays fully on.

Dispersion is the change in delay with input conditions. Overdrive dispersion from 10mV to 125mV overdrive (150mV step) is typically under 1.8ns; the propagation delay vs common mode curve shows the shift with input common-mode voltage.

The part is built for low phase noise and jitter, for turning small high-frequency sine waves into full-logic square waves with little added jitter. Jitter is given against input amplitude in the curves and against frequency in the electrical tables.

At these speeds poor layout causes output oscillation. Low-impedance planes, above all for VDD and VEE, reduce supply bounce, which grows with higher output supply. Keep input and output traces apart, or guard them with a ground or supply trace tied to the board's supply terminal rather than the part's pins. Bypass each positive supply to VEE with 2.2µF in parallel with several low-ESL, low-ESR 100nF capacitors right at the pins; a few nH of trace can put hundreds of mV on the supply at each edge. Where VEE is not ground, also bypass VEE to the ground plane the same way. Do not put capacitors between the separate input and output positive supplies, as output switching then couples into the inputs. Plan the load current's return path; if the load's return point is on the board, bypass VEE to it with 2.2µF and 100nF. Shield output traces with a ground plane to cut EMI; the complementary outputs of the LTC6752-3 give first-order EMI cancellation.

With a slowly moving input even 1mV of ground bounce can make the output oscillate through the transition. For such inputs leave internal hysteresis on (do not take LE/HYST high); raising hysteresis with LE/HYST or with positive feedback adds further noise immunity.

In the clock restoration circuit an LTC6752-2 turns a distorted 150mVP-P, 200MHz signal at 2.5V common mode into a full 1.8V output. AC coupling could be used at the input; DC coupling keeps the duty-cycle information, and the wide common-mode range makes that possible.
